$comment: Margin Agent plugin. This is the OUTPUT of the Margin Integration Skill run against the synthetic 'Nova' fixture Agent: a data-only descriptor that Margin validates against the Agent Descriptor Spec and composes into a reader from its own catalogue. No code, no expressions, no eval. See README.md.
label: Nova
$comment_home: Ordered candidates, resolved against the real filesystem at install time. The first that exists AND passes `probe` wins, so one file fits machines that keep Nova in different places.
$comment_capabilities: Sessions plus transcript-derived execution status. `quota`, `apiUsage`, `subscriptionQuota` and `handoff` are deliberately false: Nova exposes them only behind a credentialed endpoint and its own handoff distiller, neither of which the declarative catalogue can express. Declaring them without a declared reader is a validation error, which is the point: a capability is never claimed without wiring.
$comment_sessions: Nova keeps one directory per rollout under {home}/sessions and one append-only events.jsonl per rollout. The directory name is an opaque rollout folder, NOT the session id: the native id is a field inside the transcript. Every projection field below reads a NATIVE value out of the record stream, so nothing is inferred from a path or a file mtime.

sessions.$comment_identity: Nova's native identity is `session.id` on the `session.start` record. Reading it from the record (rather than `directoryName`) is what lets the Board show the id the Agent itself uses, even though the rollout directory is named differently.
sessions.$comment_timestamps: Nova records its own start and end instants. These are native timestamps, not file-write times, so the Board orders sessions by when they actually ran.
sessions.$comment_workspace: Nova records the working directory natively on its session header. This is a `record` extractor, not `scanAbsolutePaths`: the workspace is stated by the Agent, never recovered from transcript text.

$comment_executionStatus: Nova writes a native `finishReason` on every assistant turn. The last assistant turn wins; `stop` is a completed turn, `tool_use` is a turn still driving tools, `error` is a native failure marker, `cancelled` is a user stop and therefore a known non-error rest state. Any raw value not in the map yields `unknown`, never a guessed status.
$comment_probe: Structural check: does a candidate directory actually look like a Nova home? Without it, a mistyped path is indistinguishable from an Agent with no sessions.
